questions.question: What is the minimum age prescribed for a person to be eligible to become Vice-President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**35 years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The minimum age prescribed for a person to be eligible to become the Vice-President of India is **35 years**.
 
• This requirement is specified in Article 66 of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament.
 
• The Vice-President also serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• In the event of the President's death, resignation, or removal, the Vice-President can act as President until a new President is duly elected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Vice-President can be removed from office by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an absolute majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following is a colourless liquid whose formula is CHCI₃, which evaporates rapidly and turns into gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroform**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chloroform** is a colourless liquid with the chemical formula **CHCl3**.
 
• It evaporates rapidly and turns into gas at room temperature.
 
• Chloroform is used as a solvent and was historically used as an anesthetic.
 
• It has a distinct sweet smell and is denser than water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chloroform is not flammable, but it can form toxic gases when exposed to high temperatures.
 
• Prolonged exposure to chloroform can have harmful health effects, including liver and kidney damage.
 
• In modern times, the use of chloroform as an anesthetic has been discontinued due to its potential toxicity and the availability of safer alternatives.

questions.question: Why is it always emphasised NOT to touch any electric switch board with wet hands?

options.text: Combination of water and our body is a good conductor of electricity.
Wet hands can fade away the colour coat of the switchboard.
Wet hands might slip from the switch.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Combination of water and our body is a good conductor of electricity.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Combination of water and our body is a good conductor of electricity.** Water, especially when it contains dissolved salts, can significantly lower the resistance of our skin, making it easier for electricity to pass through our body.
 
• This increased conductivity can lead to severe electric shocks if one touches an electric switchboard with wet hands.
 
• Electric shocks can cause serious injuries or even be fatal, which is why it is always emphasized to avoid handling electrical appliances or switchboards with wet hands.
 
• Ensuring that your hands are dry before touching any electrical equipment can prevent these dangerous situations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Safety precautions** should always be taken when dealing with electricity to prevent accidents.
 
• Using insulated tools and wearing rubber-soled shoes can provide additional protection when working with electrical systems.
 
• Regular maintenance and inspection of electrical systems can help identify potential hazards before they cause harm.
 
• In case of an electric shock, it is crucial to disconnect the power source immediately and seek medical attention.
 
• Educating oneself about basic electrical safety can go a long way in preventing accidents.

questions.question: It is difficult to carry a heavy shopping bag with thin handles by hand, but slightly easier when the handles are covered with a thick piece of cloth. What is the reason behind that?

options.text: Increase in surface area reduces the force exerted

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increase in surface area reduces the force exerted**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carrying a heavy shopping bag with thin handles can be uncomfortable because the force exerted is concentrated over a smaller surface area, increasing pressure on the hand.
 
• When the handles are covered with a thick piece of cloth, the surface area in contact with the hand increases.
 
• **Increase in surface area reduces the force exerted** on any single point, making it easier and more comfortable to carry the bag.
 
• This principle is based on the relationship between force, pressure, and surface area: Pressure = Force / Area.
 
• By increasing the area, the pressure exerted on the hand is reduced, leading to less discomfort.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding this concept can help in designing more ergonomic handles for bags and other items that require carrying.
 
• This principle is also applied in various fields such as material science, engineering, and ergonomics to enhance comfort and reduce strain.
 
• Other examples include the use of wide straps in backpacks and cushioned handles in tools.

questions.question: A cricket ball of mass 160 grams was dropped from a height of 50 metres. What would be its kinetic energy just before touching the ground? [use the value of acceleration due to gravity as 10 m/s²]
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Potential Energy (P.E.): The energy stored in a body when work is done against gravity. It is given as:

P.E. = m × g × h

 
• When an object is dropped from a height, its potential energy is converted into kinetic energy (K.E.) just before it touches the ground.

Kinetic Energy (K.E.):__ The energy possessed by an object due to its motion. Just before hitting the ground, the kinetic energy of the object will be equal to the initial potential energy.

K.E. = P.E. = m × g × h

__
 
• Where m is mass, g is the acceleration due to gravity, and h is the height from which the object is dropped.

**Calculations:**__

Given that, m = 160 grams = 0.16 kg (since 1 kg = 1000 grams), h = 50 meters, g = 10 m/s²

So we have the formula for kinetic energy just before touching the ground:

K.E. = m × g × h = 0.16 × 10 × 50 = 80 J

**So, the kinetic energy just before touching the ground is 80 joules.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When a force is applied to an object which causes displacement along the direction of force then the work is said to be done by that force.
 
• The work done by a force is defined as: The product of the component of the applied force on the block in the direction of the displacement and the magnitude of this displacement is called work done.

i.e., W = vec F.dvec x = Fdxcos theta 

or in terms of magnitude, it can be given as

 W = F × s

where F = force applied in Newton and s = Displacement in meters.

questions.question: Which freedom is protected by Article 19(d) of the Constitution?

options.text: Freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India
Freedom to reside and settle in any part of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 19(d)** of the Constitution of India guarantees the **freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India**.
 
• This freedom is one of the six fundamental freedoms provided under Article 19, which are essential for the functioning of a democratic society.
 
• Other freedoms under Article 19 include freedom of speech and expression, freedom to assemble peacefully, freedom to form associations or unions, freedom to reside and settle in any part of India, and freedom to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business.
 
• The freedom to move freely ensures that citizens can travel and reside in any part of the country without unnecessary restrictions, promoting national unity and integration.
 
• However, reasonable restrictions can be imposed on this freedom in the interest of the general public or for the protection of the interests of any Scheduled Tribe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 19** is a part of the fundamental rights enshrined in the Constitution of India, ensuring the protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
 
• These rights are considered essential for the development of the individual and the preservation of human dignity.
 
• The Constitution of India, adopted on **26th November 1949** and effective from **26th January 1950**, is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It establishes the framework for the political principles, structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

questions.question: The Project Great Indian Bustard was launched by the Government of _______ in June 2013.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Project Great Indian Bustard** was launched by the Government of Rajasthan in June 2013.
 
• The project aims to conserve the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard, which is native to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The Great Indian Bustard is one of the heaviest flying birds in the world and is known for its distinctive black crown on the forehead contrasting with the pale head and neck.
 
• Rajasthan has been a significant habitat for this species, particularly in the Desert National Park located in the state.
 
• The project involves habitat improvement, breeding programs, and community participation to ensure the survival of this species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Great Indian Bustard is listed in Schedule I of the Indian Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and is classified as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
 
• Conservation efforts are crucial as the population of the Great Indian Bustard has been declining due to habitat loss, hunting, and other anthropogenic pressures.
 
• The Government of India has also included the Great Indian Bustard in its species recovery program under the Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats.
 
• Internationally, the bird is protected under the Convention on Migratory Species (CMS) and the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

questions.question: Which of the following is the chemical formula of baking soda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NaHCO3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NaHCO3** is the chemical formula of baking soda.
 
• Baking soda is also known as **sodium bicarbonate**.
 
• It is commonly used in baking as a **leavening agent**.
 
• When it reacts with an acid, it produces carbon dioxide gas, which helps the dough rise.
 
• Other common uses include **cleaning, deodorizing, and in medical applications** to relieve heartburn and acid indigestion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Na2CO3.10H2O** is the chemical formula for washing soda, also known as sodium carbonate decahydrate.
 
• **NaOH** is the chemical formula for sodium hydroxide, commonly known as caustic soda or lye.
 
• **CaOCl2** is the chemical formula for bleaching powder, also known as calcium oxychloride.
 
• Baking soda is different from baking powder, which contains baking soda along with an acidifying agent and a drying agent.

questions.question: The Government launched a 'Scheme for Expansion and Modernisation of Fire Services in the States' in July 2023 under the ________ for strengthening fire services in the States.

• It is managed by the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.

• The fund's utilization is overseen by the National Executive Committee (NEC) under the Chairmanship of the Union Home Secretary.

• Effective utilization of the NDRF is essential for mitigating the impact of disasters and ensuring rapid recovery.

questions.question: Which disease causes bone pain, stunted growth and soft, weak bones that can lead to skeletal deformities due to not having enough vitamin D?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rickets**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rickets** is a disease that causes bone pain, stunted growth, and soft, weak bones that can lead to skeletal deformities due to not having enough vitamin D.
 
• Vitamin D is crucial for the absorption of calcium and phosphate from the gastrointestinal tract, which are essential for healthy bone formation.
 
• Rickets is most commonly seen in children who have severe vitamin D deficiency.
 
• Common symptoms of rickets include delayed growth, pain in the spine, pelvis, and legs, muscle weakness, and skeletal deformities such as bowed legs or thickened wrists and ankles.
 
• The condition can be prevented by ensuring adequate intake of vitamin D through diet and exposure to sunlight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin D** can be obtained from foods such as fatty fish, fortified dairy products, and cereals, as well as through skin synthesis upon exposure to sunlight.
 
• In severe cases, vitamin D supplements may be prescribed to correct the deficiency.
 
• Other conditions that can cause similar symptoms include osteomalacia in adults, which also results from vitamin D deficiency but affects mature bones.
 
• Regular check-ups and maintaining a balanced diet with adequate nutrients are essential for bone health.

questions.question: Some simple multicellular organisms reproduce by first splitting into multiple pieces. Then each of these pieces grow up into a new individual. What is this method of reproduction known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fragmentation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fragmentation** is a method of asexual reproduction where an organism splits into multiple pieces, and each piece grows into a new individual.
 
• This type of reproduction is common in some simple multicellular organisms such as certain algae, fungi, and invertebrates.
 
• The process ensures rapid multiplication and colonization of new areas.
 
• It is different from **binary fission** and **multiple fission**, which are methods of reproduction in single-celled organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regeneration** is a process where organisms can regrow lost or damaged parts, but it is not primarily a method of reproduction.
 
• **Binary fission** is a common method of reproduction in prokaryotes where the organism divides into two equal parts.
 
• **Multiple fission** involves the division of the nucleus followed by the division of the cytoplasm, resulting in multiple offspring from a single parent organism.
 
• Fragmentation is advantageous in stable environments where rapid population increase is beneficial.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are Pteridophyta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fern**__

__
 
• **Fern** is classified under the division Pteridophyta.
 
• Pteridophyta, also known as ferns and their relatives, are vascular plants that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers.
 
• They are among the oldest groups of plants on Earth, with a history dating back hundreds of millions of years.
 
• Unlike mosses and liverworts, which are non-vascular, ferns have a well-developed vascular system for the transport of water and nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mosses** are non-vascular plants belonging to the division Bryophyta.
 
• **Hornworts** belong to the division Anthocerotophyta and are also non-vascular.
 
• **Lichens** are not classified under any plant division; they are a symbiotic association between a fungus and an alga or cyanobacterium.
 
• Ferns are commonly found in a variety of habitats, including moist, shaded forest floors, rocky crevices, and even tropical regions.
 
• They play a significant role in the ecosystem, including soil formation and providing habitats for other organisms.

__
 
• The Non-Cooperation Movement was called off by **Mahatma Gandhi** in response to the Chauri Chaura incident.
 
• The Chauri Chaura incident occurred on **February 4, 1922**, when a large group of protesters participating in the Non-Cooperation Movement clashed with police, resulting in the death of three civilians and 22 policemen.
 
• Gandhi was deeply disturbed by the violence and felt that the movement had deviated from its non-violent path.
 
• He believed that the country was not ready for a non-violent struggle and called off the movement to prevent further violence.
 
• The decision was met with mixed reactions; while some leaders supported Gandhi's stance, others felt that it was a setback to the freedom struggle.

• The **Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by the Indian National Congress under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi** in **1920**.
 
• It aimed to resist British rule in India through non-violent means, including the boycott of British goods, institutions, and services.
 
• The movement gained massive support and was one of the first large-scale movements of the Indian independence struggle.
 
• Despite its premature end, the Non-Cooperation Movement succeeded in uniting millions of Indians against British rule and set the stage for future movements.
 
• The Chauri Chaura incident highlighted the challenges of **maintaining non-violence in mass movements and influenced Gandhi's strategies** in subsequent campaigns.

questions.question: According to which of the following constitutional articles in India does the government need to present the estimated receipts and expenditures before the parliament?

__
 
• According to **Article 112** of the Indian Constitution, the government is required to present the estimated receipts and expenditures before the Parliament.
 
• This presentation is known as the **Annual Financial Statement** or the Budget.
 
• The Budget is a crucial document that outlines the government's fiscal policy and priorities for the upcoming financial year.
 
• It includes details of revenue and capital expenditure, along with estimates of receipts from taxes and other sources.
 
• The Budget is presented annually by the Finance Minister in the Parliament, usually on the last working day of February.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Annual Financial Statement** is divided into three parts: **the Consolidated Fund of India, the Contingency Fund of India, and the Public Account of India**.
 
• The Consolidated Fund is the most important of the three, comprising all revenues received by the government, loans raised by it, and money received in repayment of loans.
 
• The Contingency Fund is used for urgent or unforeseen expenditure, and the Public Account deals with transactions relating to debt, deposits, and advances.
 
• After the Budget is presented, it goes through a series of discussions and approvals in both Houses of Parliament before it is enacted.
 
• The Budget has a significant impact on the economy, influencing inflation, employment, investment, and overall economic growth.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1, 3 and 4**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **President** in a Parliamentary form of government, such as India, is the **nominal or de jure executive**. This means that the President is the ceremonial head of state with duties largely bound by the advice of the Prime Minister and the cabinet. ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the **head of government** and exercises most executive powers. The Prime Minister leads the executive branch of the government, formulates policies, and directs the administration. ***Hence, Statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The **President** is indeed the **head of state** in a Parliamentary form of government, serving as the nation's highest representative. ***Hence, Statement 3 is correct.***
 
• However, the Prime Minister is not the titular executive; that role is held by the President. The Prime Minister is the actual executive authority. ***Hence, Statement 2 is not correct.***

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1: Only 1, 3, and 4.**

questions.question: What is the primary reason for a government to implement a Goods and Services Tax (GST)?

options.text: To discourage all kinds of consumption
To increase the complexity of the tax system

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To simplify the tax structure**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **To simplify the tax structure** is the primary reason for a government to implement a **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**.
 
• GST aims to unify multiple indirect taxes under a single tax regime, making it easier for businesses and consumers.
 
• It helps in reducing the cascading effect of taxes, where a tax is levied on top of another tax.
 
• GST promotes a more transparent and efficient tax system, contributing to better compliance and revenue collection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** was introduced in India on **1st July 2017**.
 
• It replaced multiple indirect taxes such as VAT, service tax, excise duty, and others, creating a single unified tax system.
 
• GST is categorized into three types: **CGST (Central GST), SGST (State GST), and IGST (Integrated GST)**.
 
• CGST and SGST are levied on intra-state transactions, while IGST is levied on inter-state transactions.
 
• The introduction of GST has significantly improved the ease of doing business in India by streamlining the tax process.

questions.question: Which is the essential non-justiciable feature of the Indian Constitution associated with the welfare and well-being of the common man?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive principles of State Policy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in citation while framing laws and policies.
 
• These principles are considered essential in the governance of the country and aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are **not enforceable by any court**, but the principles laid down are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• They are mentioned in **Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51**.
 
• The Directive Principles emphasize the establishment of a welfare state where the government works towards ensuring the well-being of its citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Directive Principles** are inspired by the **Irish Constitution** and aim at providing social and economic democracy.
 
• These principles act as a yardstick in the hands of the electorate to measure the performance of the government.
 
• Some of the important Directive Principles include the right to adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work for both men and women, and the provision of free legal aid.
 
• Although non-justiciable, these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and **aim to ensure that the state strives to promote the welfare of the people**.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** added several new Directive Principles to the Indian Constitution, emphasizing the importance of these guidelines in the governance of the country.
